==Problem==

The coordinates of <imath>\triangle ABC</imath> are <imath>A(5,7)</imath>, <imath>B(11,7)</imath>, and <imath>C(3,y)</imath>, with <imath>y>7</imath>. The area of <imath>\triangle ABC</imath> is 12. What is the value of <imath>y</imath>?

<asy>

draw((3,11)--(11,7)--(5,7)--(3,11));

dot((5,7));
label("$A(5,7)$",(5,7),S);

dot((11,7));
label("$B(11,7)$",(11,7),S);

dot((3,11));
label("$C(3,y)$",(3,11),NW);

</asy>


<imath>\textbf{(A) }8\qquad\textbf{(B) }9\qquad\textbf{(C) }10\qquad\textbf{(D) }11\qquad \textbf{(E) }12</imath>

==Solution 1==
Since the triangle has a base of <imath>6</imath>, we can plug in that value as the base. Then, we can solve the equation for the height. Doing so gives us, 
<cmath>\dfrac{6h}{2}=3h=12.</cmath>
This means that <imath>h=4</imath>, so that means that we have to add 4 to the <imath>y</imath>-coordinate. So the answer is <imath>7+4=\boxed{(D) 11}</imath>

==Solution 2==
By the Shoelace Theorem, <imath>\triangle ABC</imath> has area <cmath>\frac{1}{2}|(y \cdot 11 + 7 \cdot 5 + 7 \cdot 3) - (3 \cdot 7 + 11 \cdot 7 + 5 \cdot y)| = \frac{1}{2}|(11y + 56) - (98 + 5y)| = \frac{1}{2}|6y - 42|.</cmath> From the problem, this is equal to <imath>12</imath>. We now solve for y.

<imath>\frac{1}{2}|6y - 42| = 12</imath>

<imath>|6y-42| = 24</imath>

<imath>6y - 42 = 24</imath> OR <imath>6y - 42 = -24</imath>

<imath>6y = 66</imath> OR <imath>6y = 18</imath>

<imath>y = 11</imath> OR <imath>y = 3</imath>

However, since, as stated in the problem, <imath>y > 7</imath>, our only valid solution is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)} 11}</imath>.

~ [https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/User:Cxsmi cxsmi]

==Solution 3==
As in the figure, the triangle is determined by the vectors <imath>\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ y-7\end{bmatrix}</imath> and <imath>\begin{bmatrix}6\\0\end{bmatrix}</imath>. Recall that the absolute value of the determinant of these vectors is the area of the parallelogram determined by those vectors; the triangle has half the area of that parallelogram. Then we must have that <imath>\frac{1}{2}|\begin{vmatrix}-2 & y-7\\6 & 0\end{vmatrix}| = 12 \implies \begin{vmatrix}-2 & y-7\\6 & 0\end{vmatrix} = \pm 24</imath>. Expanding the determinants, we find that <imath>-6(y-7) = 24</imath> or <imath>-6(y-7) = -24</imath>. Solving each equation individually, we find that <imath>y = 3</imath> or <imath>y = 11</imath>. However, the problem states that <imath>y > 7</imath>, so the only valid solution is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)} 11}</imath>.

~ [https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/User:Cxsmi cxsmi] (again!)

==Solution 4==
Draw a rectangle so that the hypotenuse is the diagonal of the rectangle. The base is 8 and the height is \( y - 7 \), so the area is
<imath>{8(y - 7) = 8y - 56}</imath>

Inside the rectangle, there are 2 extra right triangles along with the original triangle. The larger right triangle has an area of half the rectangle, so it has an area of

<imath>{\frac{8y - 56}{2} = 4y - 28}</imath>

The smaller right triangle has a base of 2 and a height of \( y - 7 \), so its area is

<imath>{\frac{2(y - 7)}{2} = y - 7}</imath>

Subtracting the extra right triangles from the area of the rectangle, you get

<imath>{(8y - 56) - (4y - 28) - (y - 7) = 3y - 21}</imath>

Since the problem told us that the original triangle had an area of 12, you get the equation

<imath>{3y - 21 = 12}</imath>

<imath>{3y = 33}</imath>

<imath>{y = 11}</imath>

So the answer to the problem is \( \boxed{\textbf{D}} \).


==Solution 5== 

If the area of <imath>\triangle ABC</imath> is <imath>12</imath>, then the base times height must be equal to <imath>24</imath>. We can see that the base is equal to <imath>6</imath>, subtracting the smaller x value from the larger x value of the two coordinates. So the change of the <imath>y</imath> value from point <imath>A</imath> to point <imath>C</imath> must be <imath>4</imath>. Adding <imath>4</imath> to point <imath>A</imath>'s y value gives us <imath>11</imath>, so the answer is <imath>C</imath>.
